The task is E_T=sup_[0,T] D(U_H(t)|psi><psi|U_H(t)^*,U_K(t)|psi><psi|U_K(t)^*). Unknown entries, real-time evolution, inverse dilation and arbitrary-flag unitary completion are absent. Arbitrary known candidate preparations/projectors are additional resources, not ordinary fixed-input snapshots or Gibbs samples.

At h=1/(4M), write B=exp(-hH), C=exp(-hK), a=exp(-1/4), b=a^2 and G_r=[(1-r)I+(r/b)C]^-1 with eigenvalues in [b,1]. Uniform independent s in [0,T], r in [0,1] specify v=G_r exp(-isK)psi/||G_r exp(-isK)psi||. Filter (|0>v+|1>psi)/sqrt(2); both branches experience H. Project the successful output onto the known corresponding C-filtered pair. Retry the SAME setting until success to avoid unknown setting bias; success>=exp(-1/2). Mean rejection pbar is proposed to certify E_T<=min{1,Cstar MT sqrt(pbar)}, Cstar=27.35248...<28. N independent successful shots with zero rejects give soundness-alpha bound 28MT sqrt(log(1/alpha)/N), not a Bayesian correctness probability. Norm-one observables then differ by <=2epsilon simultaneously on this one trajectory.

The proof aligns all filtered inputs with c=<psi,Bpsi>/<psi,Cpsi>, bounds ||(B/c-C)v|| by a constant times sqrt(p(v)), applies the exact ordered noncommutative resolvent integral for log(B/c)-log C, and bounds the residual along the proposed trajectory by Duhamel and Cauchy-Schwarz. It does not identify H outside C_K(psi)=span{psi,Kpsi,...}. For T>0, pbar=0 iff the rays agree on [0,T] iff (H-K)x=kappa x on that cyclic subspace, implying all-time agreement. The common scalar is an unobservable energy shift, not a measured unknown normalization.

At confidence 2/3, MT>=2 and 0<epsilon<=1/4, the source proposes optimal worst-case raw attempt order Theta(M^2 T^2/epsilon^2) and unknown-filter duration Theta(M T^2/epsilon^2). A two-level alternative H_theta=M I/2+theta Z versus K=M I/2, theta=2epsilon/T, gives lower constants 1/144 and 1/72. The stronger canonical FORWARD isometry exposes coherent failures but grants neither inverse nor arbitrary-input unitary completion. Raw-count lower bounds allow adaptive design/quantum memory and coherent duration control; duration-weighted proof uses classically adaptive durations and average expected exposure across the hypotheses. Upper retries have constant expected overhead and a bounded high-confidence raw cap. Preparation, known-model compilation, precision and total runtime are separate. No optimal local-system n dependence or all-confidence leading constants are claimed.

The strict test has perfect ideal completeness for exact ray agreement, not tolerant completeness: a nearby trajectory can have a persistent rejection floor. Implementation bias eta changes the certificate to 28MT sqrt(p_U+eta), demanding eta=O(epsilon^2/(M^2T^2)). Coherent many-body candidate preparation and a trusted programmable filter remain acquisition obligations; bounded inverse conditioning does not supply them. Candidate discovery, generic Hamiltonian learning and validation of all initial states are outside the result.

A separate reconstructed N724 nominal family supplies a bridge to full quantum snapshots. Common Jacobi scalar moments through m-1 imply A_+^j v=A_-^j v for j<ell=(m+1)/2 in a shared polynomial-coordinate basis. For spectra [3/8,5/8], vector-tail norm<=2 exp(-3s/8)(s/8)^ell/ell!, giving snapshot D<=2sqrt(3) min{(beta/16)^ell/ell!,3^-ell} with the original reference/normalization. Return-probability gap 9/32 at 4pi m yields N>=max{9^ell,(16ell/(e beta))^(2ell)}/108 for additive 1/16 estimation. This transfers the NOMINAL isospectral family through a proved-in-source vector interface, not scalar noise constants or arbitrary perturbed isospectrality. The active theorem does not depend on this bridge. N724/N725 retain their original sources, statuses and gates; this scoped continuation is independently unreviewed.

Hamiltonian certification, Gibbs learning, resolvent logarithms, Duhamel, state comparison and known matrix-function compilation are credited antecedents.
